keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Soshangane 'extended control between the Komati (Incomati) and the Zambezi rivers' and the empire 'at its height in the 1860s, covered all of Mozambique between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers'; drawn as the five provinces south of the Zambezi (about 259,000 km2 whole by the gazetteer, about 238,000 km2 after the subtraction below; the author's earlier figure of 272,000 km2 was not the gazetteer's). The page gives no infobox area to compare; the shape is held from the 1837 defeat of Nxaba to 1895 because no loss before the 1895 collapse is dated (confidence 2). Soshangane's Zimbabwean base on the middle Sabi is not drawn. [Repair 2026-10-19: the earlier shape drew the whole of the five provinces and so overlapped portuguese-mozambique K5-K7 (the Sofala, Inhambane and Delagoa Bay posts and the 60 km Zambezi strip in Sofala province, about 21,000 km2 by the gazetteer, about 25,000 by the reviewer's estimate) for 58 years. DECISION: the posts and the strip stay Portuguese and are subtracted here. The Gaza page says only that 'Soshangane's army overran these Portuguese settlements' and never dates a later status; the Soshangane page dates the destruction of the forts (Lourenço Marques 28 October 1833, Inhambane 3 November 1834, Sofala October 1836) and says the Portuguese 'paid tribute' in the 1840s-50s, with Sena and Tete 'brought under Gaza control and forced to pay tax' (no year). No page dates a Portuguese loss or recovery of the posts, so no dated loss is entered in either dossier; the tribute is a relation, not territory.]

notes: Cliopatria has no Gaza. Budget: Gaza Empire article (opened four times for different passes) and the Gungunhana page, with a disambiguation page for Chaimite that gave nothing. The infobox says 'Independent Kingdom (1824-1882), Portuguese protectorate (1882-1895)'; the protectorate is a Portuguese-side vassal_start 1882 / vassal_end 1895 (counterpart gaza-empire) and is NOT in this ledger, because the schema puts the vassal tint on the suzerain's dossier; the portuguese-mozambique dossier carries it. Not settled: the date of the Limpopo crossing; the 1830 subjugation year (page silent, confidence 1); the Zimbabwean part of Soshangane's realm (the page puts his capital 'in the highlands of the middle Sabi River' in present-day Zimbabwe, Today part of: 'Mozambique Zimbabwe South Africa'); the flight of Mzila's followers to the Soutpansberg ('to leave Mozambique and flee to the Soutpansberg Mountains in the Transvaal'); the 1884-85 and 1890-91 treaties (not on the pages). Capital coordinates are stand-ins. Counterpart names: Nxaba's Ngoni kingdom (a short-lived state inland from Sofala, 1830s). Gazetteer: names resolve (admin1 Gaza, Inhambane, Maputo, Sofala, Manica of Mozambique). REPAIR 2026-10-19 (after review): (1) OVERLAP WITH portuguese-mozambique SETTLED: the Portuguese posts (Inhambane 25 km, Delagoa Bay 40 km, Sofala 30 km) and the 60 km Zambezi strip in Sofala province are subtracted from the Gaza keyframes and from the ledger regions; portuguese-mozambique keeps them (K5-K7) and enters no loss, because no page dates a later Gaza or Portuguese hold. The Soshangane page says the forts were destroyed in 1833-1836 and the Portuguese then paid tribute (1840s-50s); the Gaza page says only 'overran'. (2) The coast gain is dated 1834 (was 1830) and the keyframe split at 1834. (3) Capital for 1824-1827 added from the Soshangane page. (4) Disagreement between pages: the Soshangane page puts Nxaba's removal at 1835 and Soshangane's lower Limpopo residence at 1827-1835/6; the Gaza page gives 1837 for Nxaba and the infobox Chaimite 1828-1834. The Gaza page's date is kept for /ledger/2.
